threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: Use after free needs manual deallocation. JavaScript has none, but ArrayBuffer detachment and native addons are the escape routes. V8 is a garbage-collected, bounds-checked runtime, so these classes cannot corrupt memory from pure JavaScript; the exclusion holds only for a package that reaches no native code, WebAssembly or shared memory, which an analyzer must check (registry subset gc_runtimes). Engine and JIT bugs are outside the package and stated, not hidden.

threats.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
threats.rationale: andN, orN and xorN take a rest parameter whose length the caller chooses and loop over it (gates.ts:593-602, 614-623, 663-674); cost is linear in that length and the rest array is allocated by the call. The two-input gates are constant time. A huge spread (andN(...a) with millions of elements) either takes linear time or fails with an engine RangeError (stack size), which carries the same class as the gates' rejection (see typescript.engine-rangeerror-identity).

Runs in BUILD (npx vitest run --coverage) but no repository tool reads the result at report time.

threats.name: Negative zero accepted as the bit 0 (IEEE-754 comparison pitfall)
threats.rationale: -0 === 0 in JavaScript, so a check written value !== 0 && value !== 1 lets -0 through as a valid bit, and it prints as "0". threats.name: Numeric truncation by the 32-bit bitwise operators and shifts
threats.rationale: JavaScript converts the operands of <<, >>, >>>, &, | and ^ to 32-bit integers and takes shift counts modulo 32: 2^32 + 1 & 1 is 1, 1 << 32 is 1, 1 << 31 is negative. The 31-and-more-bit wrong results were fixed by PR #19958 (merged). The operators are present but bounded, and a syntactic rule still flags them.

threats.name: Wrong number of arguments (JavaScript ignores extras and fills missing with undefined)
threats.rationale: A JavaScript function can be called with any number of arguments. The two- and one-input gates check arguments.length (gates.ts:99-103, 140, 173 and so on) so a third wire is a TypeError. mux and dmux (gates.ts:720-751) have no arity check, so mux(0, 1, 0, 99) and dmux(1, 0, 5) silently ignore the extra argument; andN, orN and xorN are variadic by design. A missing argument arrives as undefined and is rejected by validateBit. Variadic gates differ: andN and orN reject fewer than 2 inputs with RangeError (gates.ts:594-596, 615-617), the same error identity as value rejection (so the arity failure is a RangeError while the two-input gates report arity as TypeError, and it widens the collision with the engine's own RangeError, see typescript.engine-rangeerror-identity); xorN accepts 0 and 1 inputs (gates.ts:663-672, returns the XOR identity 0 for none).

threats.name: The gates' RangeError is not distinguishable from an engine RangeError
threats.rationale: The rejection identity for an out-of-range integer is the general-purpose RangeError (LG02 section 7). The engine raises the same class for call-stack exhaustion (a huge spread into andN), invalid array length and others, and the lane binding matches the class only. LG02 section 7 names this residual risk. The corpus catches a misfire on a valid input (it expects a value), not a RangeError for the wrong reason on an invalid input. andN and orN also use RangeError for too few inputs (gates.ts:594-596, 615-617), so an arity failure and a value failure share one identity.

threats.name: The suite can pass vacuously or on one engine only
threats.rationale: vitest run exits 0 with it.skip, it.only or an empty loop; the only gate is a lines>=80 coverage threshold (vitest.config.ts:7-9). The tests run on whichever Node the CI image has; no engines field (package.json) and no run on a second engine (V8 versus JavaScriptCore or SpiderMonkey) exist, although ECMAScript leaves error message text and some number formatting implementation-defined (the library never reads a message). CWE mapping: CWE-758 (reliance on undefined, unspecified or implementation-defined behavior) fits the engine-variance half only (ECMAScript leaves error message text and some formatting implementation-defined); the vacuous-suite half (it.skip, it.only, an empty loop) has no precise CWE and is described by the row text, not by a mapping.
